title: Scoped negative result: four R420 triple-basis escapes exceed precision
body:
At one fixed R420 decoder, no single restored helper shear saves an ADD, but exactly four three-helper basis changes save one decoder ADD, or two in the complete word. Every escape needs a 105-bit positive-prefix bill and fails the inherited native condition `64 F^3 B^2 < 2^104`. This is a scoped negative result with explicit correct XOR witnesses, not a new supplier admission or kappa.

The new evidence is a complete `82,160 triples × 168 GL(3,2) matrices = 13,802,880` census after a precisely recorded single-shear fixed point. A matrix-column implementation and a separate eight-input truth-table implementation agree on the full gain histogram and every positive matrix. All four positive matrices have unique shortest preparation/restoration words. Since each saves exactly one, any longer realization loses its strict saving. The proof therefore covers arbitrary finite sequence lengths within this fixed-prefix, closed three-helper class.

All seven reconstructed words pass the original E8/frame/H1-H5 checker and a separate complete 660-column dirty-input interpreter. An independent sparse integer-matrix replay of the unchanged exporter's actual records confirms all fourteen positive bounds, COPY/ERASE lifetimes and unchanged paid histogram. Ten failure controls pass. Failing the inherited upper bill does not prove actual arithmetic overflow.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/r420-triple-bases-seed01
```

Expected `PASS_R420_TRIPLE_BASES_PRECISION_BOUNDARY`, `PASS_R420_TRIPLE_LITERAL_RECORDS` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The registered replay, an isolated Python 3.11 replay from outside the checkout, five selected-record tests, selected-source integrity, Python 3.10 grammar and whitespace checks pass. C++ native multistage execution, complete hosting, selected cold replay, Linux, Lean and human review were not run; hosted CI success is not asserted.

Only `research/r420-triple-bases-seed01/` is added. Research base is `e6f9716621f4e01fc190617934cdfaf072bd976f`; rebased onto `ef5f39403610d231a0c27e8a6b4f08c10209bcd6` with all consumed inputs and rules unchanged. OS seed01, bit-supplier track. No pinned sprint issue existed, so the claim is local. The final refresh covered 750 open PR bodies and 182 discussion records; a failed helper refresh was replaced by a successful direct PR query and is disclosed in VALIDATION.json.

Credit Adam Gall's PR1206 at `3c0a3240035f1c71ef09251b7be7c4791da8157d`, Sagar Thakrar's PR708/753, eumemic's PR543, Dylan Crow's exporter and the retained construction lineage. PR748 has larger overall savings through a changed source/D map; no circuit record is claimed. PR1306's zero-frame target-feedback model is distinct. The exact fixed-prefix scope, both native and stricter PR1206-wrapper precision predicates, source pins and next question are in README.md.

Prepared for Sagar Thakrar (@thakrarsagar) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, proof, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0. Inherited compiler/realization, hosting, precision/tape and analytic obligations remain.
